scenario_text: A uniformly charged, nonconducting sphere is placed in vacuum, with its total charge and radius varied between trials. The radial electric field is sampled at points that may lie inside or outside the sphere. The target is the signed outward field component, so the model must capture the change from a regular interior profile to exterior geometric decay. The charge distribution is prescribed and no charge motion is modeled.

spec.target_description: signed radial electric field component at the observation radius, in volts per meter

input_symbols.description: total charge of the sphere, in coulombs
sphere radius, in meters
radial observation coordinate, in meters

expected_behaviors: Near the center, the field approaches zero and its magnitude grows linearly with radius.
The field is continuous across the sphere surface.
Outside the sphere, the magnitude has inverse-square distance decay.
Reversing the total charge reverses the signed field.
forbidden_behaviors: A singular field at the center.
A jump in the field at the sphere surface.
A nonzero response when the total charge is zero.
Angular or time dependence for the spherical static source.

scenario_text: A thin circular wire loop carries a steady prescribed current in vacuum. Its radius and signed axial observation coordinate are varied, and the target is the axial magnetic flux density. The response must capture the finite central field and the geometric falloff far from the loop. The current source is ideal, and no circuit transient is included.

spec.target_description: signed axial magnetic flux density produced by the current loop, in teslas

input_symbols.description: signed loop current, in amperes
loop radius, in meters
signed axial observation coordinate, in meters

expected_behaviors: The field reverses when the current reverses.
The axial field is unchanged when the sign of the observation coordinate is reversed.
For fixed radius and current, the field magnitude is finite and largest at the loop center.
Far from the loop, the field magnitude falls with the third power of axial distance.
forbidden_behaviors: A singularity at the loop center.
Odd dependence on the axial observation coordinate.
A nonzero field when the current is zero.
Time dependence from a steady current source.

scenario_text: An idealized isotropic magnetic medium is held at fixed temperature in a reversible, history-independent regime. A signed uniform magnetizing field is applied along one axis, and the equilibrium magnetization along that axis is measured. Magnetic dipole alignment gives a nearly linear weak-field response that smoothly approaches fixed positive or negative plateaus. Domain history, heating, and hysteresis are excluded.

spec.target_description: signed equilibrium magnetization along the applied-field axis, in amperes per meter

input_symbols.description: signed applied magnetizing field, in amperes per meter

expected_behaviors: The response is approximately linear for weak applied fields.
The magnetization changes sign when the applied field changes sign.
The magnitude approaches a finite material-dependent plateau at strong fields.
The response is smooth, monotonic, and single-valued.
forbidden_behaviors: Unbounded magnetization at strong fields.
Hysteresis or dependence on previous field values.
Nonzero remanent magnetization at zero applied field.
Oscillatory or discontinuous switching behavior.

scenario_text: Two coherent, collinear monochromatic plane waves with the same frequency and polarization overlap in vacuum. Their electric-field amplitudes and relative phase are varied independently while the propagation geometry remains fixed. The target is the cycle-averaged electromagnetic energy flux at the overlap point. Only coherent field superposition is modeled; detector dynamics and material response are absent.

spec.target_description: cycle-averaged electromagnetic intensity at the overlap point, in watts per square meter

input_symbols.description: electric-field amplitude of the first wave, in volts per meter
electric-field amplitude of the second wave, in volts per meter
relative phase between the waves, in radians

expected_behaviors: The intensity is periodic in relative phase.
Aligned phases give the largest intensity for fixed amplitudes.
For equal amplitudes, opposing phases can reduce the intensity to zero.
Interchanging the two wave amplitudes leaves the response unchanged.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative electromagnetic intensity.
Phase dependence when either wave amplitude is zero.
Dependence on the absolute phase of both waves together.
A secular or nonperiodic trend with relative phase.

scenario_text: A monochromatic plane field enters a homogeneous conducting half-space at normal incidence. The electric-field envelope immediately inside the surface is prescribed, while depth, frequency, and conductivity are varied with permeability fixed. The target is the local envelope amplitude rather than the instantaneous oscillating field. Heating and conductivity changes are excluded, leaving only conductive electromagnetic attenuation.

spec.target_description: electric-field envelope amplitude inside the conductor, in volts per meter

input_symbols.description: electric-field envelope just inside the conductor surface, in volts per meter
depth below the conductor surface, in meters
field frequency, in hertz
electrical conductivity, in siemens per meter

expected_behaviors: At the surface, the target matches the prescribed surface envelope.
The envelope decays exponentially with depth.
Higher frequency or conductivity produces stronger attenuation with depth.
The response is nonnegative and scales linearly with the surface envelope.
forbidden_behaviors: Growth of the envelope with depth.
An oscillating sign in the envelope quantity.
A nonzero deep-interior asymptote.
Dependence on the instantaneous time phase of the harmonic field.

scenario_text: An electrically small source in vacuum has a prescribed sinusoidal electric dipole moment along a fixed axis. The dipole-moment amplitude and oscillation frequency are varied while the source dimensions remain much shorter than the wavelength. The target is the cycle-averaged electromagnetic power radiated over all directions. The drive circuit and source mechanics are fixed backgrounds, so only radiation generation is modeled.

spec.target_description: total cycle-averaged electromagnetic power radiated by the dipole, in watts

input_symbols.description: electric dipole-moment amplitude, in coulomb meters
dipole oscillation frequency, in hertz

expected_behaviors: The radiated power is nonnegative.
The power scales quadratically with dipole-moment amplitude.
The power has fourth-power scaling with frequency.
The response vanishes with zero dipole-moment amplitude and approaches zero at vanishing frequency.
forbidden_behaviors: Dependence of total radiated power on observation distance.
Negative radiated power.
Linear scaling with dipole-moment amplitude.
Saturation at high frequency within the electrically small-source regime.

scenario_text: A stationary single-turn loop of area 0.01 square meter is threaded by a spatially uniform sinusoidal magnetic field normal to its plane. The field amplitude, angular frequency, and instantaneous phase are independently sampled. The target is the open-circuit terminal voltage induced around the loop at that phase. The source producing the field is prescribed, and loop current and field backreaction are excluded.

spec.target_description: signed open-circuit voltage induced around the stationary loop, in volts

input_symbols.description: magnetic flux-density amplitude, in teslas
angular frequency of the magnetic field, in radians per second
instantaneous phase of the magnetic field, in radians

expected_behaviors: The voltage varies sinusoidally with sampled phase.
The voltage is zero at extrema of the magnetic field and largest in magnitude at its zero crossings.
The voltage magnitude scales linearly with field amplitude and angular frequency.
The voltage vanishes for a static field or zero field amplitude.
forbidden_behaviors: A phase-independent direct-current offset.
A nonzero voltage from a static magnetic field.
Saturation with field amplitude in the ideal loop.
Dependence on prior phase history or an unmodeled loop current.

scenario_text: An ideal capacitor initially holds a signed voltage and discharges through a fixed 1.0 kilohm resistor, with capacitance fixed at 10 microfarads. There is no source or parasitic inductance. Over a 0.05 second window, only the capacitor voltage is evolved, and the target is its instantaneous time derivative. Heating is not a state; all dissipation is represented by the fixed resistance.

spec.target_description: time derivative of the capacitor voltage, in volts per second

required_dynamic_states.description: signed capacitor voltage, in volts

expected_behaviors: The voltage approaches zero exponentially from either sign.
The voltage derivative always opposes a nonzero capacitor voltage.
The derivative magnitude decreases as the capacitor voltage approaches zero.
Zero voltage is a stable equilibrium.
forbidden_behaviors: Oscillation or overshoot.
Spontaneous reversal of the voltage sign.
Growth away from zero without a source.
Relaxation to a nonzero voltage offset.

scenario_text: A source-free ideal series loop contains a 10 millihenry inductive element and a 10 microfarad capacitive element. Capacitor charge and loop current are jointly evolved for 0.01 seconds. The target is the current derivative as magnetic and electric field energy exchange periodically. Resistance, radiation, and component nonlinearity are absent.

spec.target_description: time derivative of the loop current, in amperes per second

required_dynamic_states.description: signed charge stored on the capacitor, in coulombs
signed current through the series loop, in amperes

expected_behaviors: Charge and current remain bounded and periodic.
Electric and magnetic field energy exchange without net loss.
Current and charge are coupled with a quarter-cycle phase relation for a pure oscillation.
The current derivative acts restoratively with respect to capacitor charge.
forbidden_behaviors: Exponential damping or growth.
Settling to a nonzero steady current.
Drift in total stored electromagnetic energy.
Independent evolution of charge and current.

scenario_text: An electron moves in spatially uniform perpendicular electric and magnetic fields in vacuum. The electric field is fixed at 2000 volts per meter along the positive x direction, and the magnetic flux density is fixed at 0.02 tesla along the positive z direction. Because the fields are uniform, the x and y velocity components are jointly evolved for 10 nanoseconds, with the x-directed acceleration as the target. Collisions, radiation loss, and field backreaction are excluded.

spec.target_description: time derivative of the electron velocity component along the x axis, in meters per second squared

required_dynamic_states.description: electron velocity component along the x axis, in meters per second
electron velocity component along the y axis, in meters per second

expected_behaviors: The two velocity components are dynamically coupled.
The velocity components oscillate around a constant transverse drift.
The target acceleration is an affine function of the transverse velocity component.
The motion is undamped, with rotation direction fixed by the electron charge and magnetic-field orientation.
forbidden_behaviors: Independent evolution of the two velocity components.
Exponential damping or runaway growth.
Dependence on particle position in spatially uniform fields.
Radiation-reaction or collision terms.

scenario_text: An ideal point mass hangs from a massless rigid link and swings in a vertical plane under uniform gravity. The angular displacement theta and angular rate omega are evolved from initial conditions, with link length and gravity fixed across trajectories. The target is angular acceleration, retaining the full finite-angle geometry rather than a small-angle approximation. The data include bounded swings and continuous rotations at sufficiently high initial energy.

spec.target_description: Angular acceleration generated by gravity during finite-angle planar swinging.

required_dynamic_states.description: Angular displacement from the downward vertical, in radians.
Angular velocity, in radians per second.

expected_behaviors: Angular acceleration is periodic in theta and directed toward the downward equilibrium.
Small excursions are nearly sinusoidal, while finite amplitudes alter the period.
Mechanical energy remains constant, and sufficiently energetic trajectories rotate continuously.
forbidden_behaviors: Using a globally linear restoring dependence on theta.
Adding damping, external driving, or random torque.
Introducing discontinuities when theta crosses an angle-wrap boundary.

scenario_text: A compact body falls vertically in a uniform gravitational field. Its downward displacement s and downward speed v evolve under fixed weight and a mechanical resistance that opposes motion and grows with the square of speed. Mass and resistance strength are fixed, and the target is downward acceleration for nonnegative speeds. Trajectories approach a finite terminal speed monotonically from either side.

spec.target_description: Downward acceleration under constant gravity and quadratic mechanical resistance.

required_dynamic_states.description: Downward displacement from the launch reference, in meters.
Downward speed, in meters per second.

expected_behaviors: Acceleration is downward below terminal speed and upward relative to the chosen coordinate above terminal speed.
Speed approaches the terminal value monotonically without crossing it.
The resistance contribution grows quadratically with speed and is independent of displacement.
forbidden_behaviors: Allowing resistance to assist downward motion.
Replacing the quadratic dependence with purely linear resistance.
Producing oscillation or overshoot around terminal speed.
Making displacement directly alter the force.

scenario_text: A particle moves in a plane around a fixed central mass. Its Cartesian position and velocity components evolve under an attractive force directed toward the center whose magnitude decreases with the square of separation. The central strength is fixed, and the target is the horizontal acceleration component. Initial conditions include both bound and escaping paths while avoiding close passage through the singular center.

spec.target_description: Horizontal acceleration caused by inverse-square central attraction.

required_dynamic_states.description: Horizontal position relative to the central mass, in benchmark length units.
Vertical position relative to the central mass, in benchmark length units.
Horizontal velocity component, in benchmark speed units.
Vertical velocity component, in benchmark speed units.

expected_behaviors: The acceleration vector always points toward the fixed center.
Acceleration magnitude decreases with the square of radial separation and has no velocity dependence.
Angular momentum and mechanical energy remain constant along nonsingular trajectories.
forbidden_behaviors: Adding drag, thrust, or a constant downward field.
Computing independent one-dimensional forces from x and y instead of using their shared radial separation.
Softening or clipping the attraction at ordinary sampled separations.

scenario_text: A mass slides without friction along a line and is attached to a symmetric nonlinear elastic element. The restoring force has both a linear contribution and a hardening cubic contribution, with mass and elastic coefficients fixed. Position x and velocity v evolve together, and the target is acceleration. Larger-amplitude cycles have shorter periods while remaining symmetric about the origin.

spec.target_description: Acceleration produced by linear and hardening cubic elastic restoration.

required_dynamic_states.description: Displacement from the elastic equilibrium, in meters.
Velocity along the line, in meters per second.

expected_behaviors: Acceleration is an odd polynomial function of displacement and points toward the origin.
Oscillations remain symmetric about the equilibrium.
Oscillation frequency increases with amplitude because of the hardening contribution.
Mechanical energy remains constant.
forbidden_behaviors: Adding damping, external forcing, or dry friction.
Introducing even displacement powers that break reflection symmetry.
Clipping or saturating the restoring force at large sampled displacement.

scenario_text: A rigid block slides along a horizontal rough surface after receiving an initial velocity, with no continuing horizontal drive. Position x and velocity v evolve under a fixed normal load and a dry contact resistance of constant magnitude opposite the direction of sliding. The target is acceleration, including the transition to a stuck state when velocity reaches zero. Trajectories begin with either sign of velocity and remain at rest after stopping.

spec.target_description: Piecewise acceleration caused by constant-magnitude dry sliding resistance and sticking at rest.

required_dynamic_states.description: Horizontal block position, in meters.
Signed horizontal velocity, in meters per second.

expected_behaviors: While sliding, acceleration has constant magnitude and opposes the sign of velocity.
Velocity reaches zero in finite time without reversing direction.
Position becomes constant after the block enters the stuck state.
forbidden_behaviors: Replacing finite-time stopping with smooth exponential decay.
Allowing velocity to cross zero and restart without an applied force.
Adding a position-dependent restoring force.
Assigning nonzero acceleration to an undriven block that is already at rest.

scenario_text: A vertically ascending vehicle expels onboard mass downward at a fixed rate and fixed relative exhaust speed in uniform gravity. Height h, upward velocity v, and remaining mass m are evolved only during the powered interval, with aerodynamic forces excluded. The target is upward acceleration produced by fixed momentum transfer acting on a decreasing mass while gravity remains constant. The time range ends before the fixed dry-mass cutoff is reached.

spec.target_description: Upward acceleration of a mass-expelling vehicle during its powered ascent.

required_dynamic_states.description: Vehicle height above the reference level, in meters.
Upward vehicle velocity, in meters per second.
Remaining vehicle mass, in kilograms.

expected_behaviors: Remaining mass decreases linearly throughout the modeled burn.
The upward recoil contribution to acceleration grows as mass decreases.
Gravity contributes a constant downward offset.
Height evolves consistently with the upward velocity.
forbidden_behaviors: Treating the vehicle mass as constant or exponentially decaying.
Applying recoil as a mass-independent fixed acceleration.
Adding aerodynamic drag or atmospheric state variables.
Extending the powered relation beyond the dry-mass cutoff.

scenario_text: A rigid body with three unequal principal inertias rotates freely with no applied torque. The three body-frame angular-velocity components evolve through inertial coupling, while the principal inertias remain fixed. The target is the time derivative of the first angular-velocity component. Trajectories include rotations near each principal axis so that stable and unstable regimes are represented.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the first body-frame angular-velocity component due to torque-free inertial coupling.

required_dynamic_states.description: Angular-velocity component about the first principal axis, in radians per second.
Angular-velocity component about the second principal axis, in radians per second.
Angular-velocity component about the third principal axis, in radians per second.

expected_behaviors: The target derivative is bilinear in the other two angular-velocity components.
Pure rotation about any one principal axis remains an exact steady motion.
Rotational kinetic energy and the magnitude of angular momentum remain constant.
Motion near the intermediate-inertia axis displays instability while the other two principal-axis regimes are stable.
forbidden_behaviors: Adding damping or an external torque.
Evolving the three components as independent oscillators.
Using equal principal inertias for the triaxial benchmark.
Allowing systematic drift in the conserved mechanical quantities.

scenario_text: Two point masses undergo an ideal instantaneous head-on impact on a frictionless line. The first approaches from the left with speed u1 and the second from the right with speed u2, while both masses are independently varied. The impact preserves total translational momentum and kinetic energy, and the target is the signed rightward outgoing velocity of the first mass. Equal-mass and extreme-mass-ratio cases expose exchange and recoil behavior.

spec.target_description: Signed rightward velocity of the first mass immediately after the lossless head-on impact.

input_symbols.description: Mass of the body approaching from the left, in kilograms.
Mass of the body approaching from the right, in kilograms.
Rightward incoming speed of the first body, in meters per second.
Leftward incoming speed of the second body, in meters per second.

expected_behaviors: For equal masses, the bodies exchange their incoming signed velocities.
Total signed momentum and total kinetic energy are unchanged by the impact.
Swapping body labels while reversing the spatial direction produces the corresponding mirrored result.
Extreme mass ratios approach the expected light-body and heavy-body recoil limits.
forbidden_behaviors: Introducing sticking, kinetic-energy loss, or a tunable restitution factor.
Making the output depend on contact duration, position, or acceleration history.
Clipping outgoing velocities at zero.
Ignoring the sign convention for the second incoming velocity.

scenario_text: Two hanging masses are connected by a massless inextensible cord over a rigid pulley with nonzero rotational inertia. The masses, pulley inertia, and pulley radius are independently varied, while gravity is fixed and the cord does not slip. The target is the downward acceleration of the second mass obtained from coupled translation and rotation. The acceleration vanishes for equal masses and is reduced in magnitude as pulley inertia increases.

spec.target_description: Signed downward acceleration of the second hanging mass.

input_symbols.description: First hanging mass, in kilograms.
Second hanging mass, in kilograms.
Pulley rotational inertia, in kilogram square meters.
Pulley radius, in meters.

expected_behaviors: The acceleration is zero when the two masses match.
Its sign reverses when the two masses are exchanged.
Increasing pulley inertia reduces the acceleration magnitude.
The pulley radius affects how rotational inertia loads the translational motion.
forbidden_behaviors: Ignoring pulley inertia or radius.
Forcing the cord tensions on both sides to be identical while the pulley accelerates.
Adding bearing friction, cord slip, or cord elasticity.
Predicting nonzero acceleration for equal masses.

scenario_text: A uniform perfectly flexible cable hangs at static equilibrium in a vertical gravitational field. Horizontal coordinate x is measured from the lowest point, where the vertical rise is zero, and the horizontal tension scale and linear mass density are independently varied. The target y is the cable's vertical rise at x, determined by distributed weight and tension balance. Profiles are symmetric, convex, and increasingly flat as horizontal tension grows.

spec.target_description: Vertical rise of the hanging cable relative to its lowest point.

input_symbols.description: Horizontal coordinate measured from the cable's lowest point, in meters.
Horizontal component of cable tension, in newtons.
Cable mass per unit length, in kilograms per meter.

expected_behaviors: Vertical rise is even in x and has its unique minimum at the center.
The profile is convex and steepens away from the lowest point.
Increasing horizontal tension flattens the profile.
Increasing linear mass density increases sag and curvature under fixed tension.
forbidden_behaviors: Using a single global parabola over the full coordinate range.
Producing asymmetric, oscillatory, or negative-rise profiles.
Adding bending stiffness or treating the cable as a rigid beam.
Making the local profile depend on unspecified endpoint dynamics.
